subject: Cardinal Health: processing locations, subprocessors, and deletion timelines
messages:
From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Victoria Mills <victoria.mills@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Quick Q: where is Cardinal data processed?

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. A few of our teams (security + procurement) want a short Q&A so we can decide if Redwood is a fit for a pilot. Can you confirm the following for requests sent to Redwood hosted inference?

1) Primary regions where inference runs (and what happens if capacity moves a request across regions)
2) Full list of subprocessors that may touch request data (including cloud provider regions)
3) How long request data may persist in caches (KV prefix cache, transient inference cache) and how that is purged on deletion requests
4) Backup/replica retention and the SLA for purging from backups after a deletion request
5) Global encryption/ KMS key locality — do keys and CMKs reside in the same region as processing?
6) Any workflow we can share with our compliance team (evidence, attestations, timeline)?

We're aiming for simple, concrete commitments (not high-level marketing). If you have a short diagram or roster you can attach that would help.

Best,
Sam
Sam Ellis
Head of Cloud Security, Cardinal Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Victoria Mills <victoria.mills@cardinalhealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where is Cardinal data processed?

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, actionable response we can share with your compliance team. I've attached a short subprocessor rollup and a residency map (see attachments). If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call to walk through any item.

1) Regions of execution - Hosted mode: requests are executed in the region you select (we default to us‑east‑1 for customers in the US unless you pin a region). We also support explicit region pinning (us‑east‑1, us‑west‑2, eu‑west‑1). If capacity requires fallback, requests are routed to the nearest compatible region by our smart router and the request will include an automated audit event noting the executed region.

2) Subprocessors (summary) - Primary cloud infra: CloudInfra Inc (AWS: us‑east‑1, us‑west‑2), NimbusCompute (GCP: europe‑west1 for EU failover), EdgeServe Ltd (edge caching nodes, us regions). - Storage/Backups: ObjectStoreCo (S3 compatible in customer region and cross‑region replication for durability). - Observability/analytics: MetricsCorp (logs scrubbed of request payloads by default).

Full rollup with regions is attached (redwood_subprocessors_rollup_v1.xlsx).

3) Caching and TTLs - KV/Prefix cache: session / prefix caches are stored in-memory on the serving nodes with a default TTL of 30 minutes and are evicted continuously; they are never written to durable disk in hosted mode unless explicit caching is enabled in your configuration.
- Transient inference cache (short lived tokenization artifacts) is ephemeral and cleared on model re‑start or node recycle. On a customer deletion request we mark the customer key and trigger cache invalidation across the fleet; most in‑memory caches become inaccessible within 24 hours and are fully invalidated in 72 hours in normal operation.

4) Backups and replicas - Backups are encrypted and stored in region by default. Our retention policy for backups is 90 days; on a verified deletion request we run a deletion workflow which removes customer data from live storage immediately and schedules backup purges. Our SLA: backups are purged within 30 days of the approved deletion request; we will provide a signed confirmation once the purge completes.

5) Encryption and KMS - Data in transit: TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS options for Private deployments.
- Data at rest: encrypted using AES‑256; KMS keys are regional by default. For Hosted customers we store CMKs in the region where processing occurs; for Dedicated/Private customers we can align key management to your KMS/HSM (bring‑your‑own‑key).

6) Evidence & workflow - We can provide: subprocessor roster (attached), residency map (attached), deletion confirmation letter, and region‑tagged audit logs (sample). We can also walk through SOC2 artifacts under NDA.

Next steps: I can set up a short call with our infra lead (Jonas) if you want deeper technical evidence or a sample audit packet.

Regards,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_rollup_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), residency_map_v2.pdf (diagram)

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where is Cardinal data processed? (technical addendum)

Adding a couple of technical clarifications from the runtime side:

- KV cache eviction & deletion propagation: when we mark a tenant for deletion we publish an invalidation event via our control plane which carries the tenant id and deletion token. All serving nodes subscribe and apply the invalidation; in practice you should expect in‑memory caches to become effectively empty within 24 hours and fully cleaned up in 72 hours (this accounts for node drains and edge caches).

- Backup purges: we run a glob purge job targeted by tenant id; purges will remove backups in the same region first. Cross‑region replicas are purged in the follow‑up phase; end‑to‑end completion depends on active replication windows but is included in the 30‑day purge SLA Hannah mentioned.

- KMS: for hosted customers we manage regional CMKs; for customers requiring key residency we recommend Dedicated or Private so you control the key material.

Happy to join the call if you want low‑level logs (audit samples) or a timeline diagram.

Jonas
Principal Infrastructure Engineer

Date: Sat, 31 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where is Cardinal data processed? — SLA blurb and logs

Sam — please find the requested short SLA + logs note below. Feel free to paste into your DPA; we can provide a slightly amended version on legal letterhead if needed.

SLA (suggested blurb): 
"Redwood Inference will remove customer request data from live serving infrastructure within 24 hours of an approved deletion request. In‑memory caches used for inference are invalidated fleet‑wide and rendered inaccessible within 24 hours and are fully cleaned within 72 hours. Encrypted backups and replicas are purged within 30 calendar days of an approved deletion request; cross‑region replicas and any subprocessor‑held copies are confirmed purged (or a plan to purge) within 45 calendar days and Redwood will provide signed confirmation upon completion."

Observability logs: by default our metrics and tracing systems do not persist unredacted request payloads. Diagnostic logs may contain metadata (request ids, timestamps, region tags). If your team requires, we can enable a strict no‑payload retention mode (suppress all request payloads from observability pipelines) or set up a short retention window for any requested diagnostic traces.

Attachments: deletion_propagation_diagram.png (illustrates invalidation + backup purge windows).

Next steps: if that SLA language looks good to procurement/legal I'll loop in our compliance counsel to produce a formal amendment. Happy to jump on a quick call Monday.

Regards,
Hannah
